publications.summary: Data on lending and deposit rates of scheduled commercial banks (SCBs) (excluding regional rural banks and small finance banks) received during October 2026 are set out in Tables 1 to 9. Highlights: Lending Rates: The weighted average lending rate (WALR) on outstanding rupee loans of SCBs remained unchanged at 8.96 per cent in September 2026 compared to August 2026. The WALR on fresh as well as outstanding rupee loans exhibited a mixed movement across sectors in September 2026. publications.title: Brits nearly twice as likely to spot pressure tactics in horror films as investment red flags
publications.summary: Investors are almost twice as likely to recognise pressure tactics in a horror film as they are when those tactics are used to promote an investment opportunity, new FCA data suggests. A survey of UK 18 to 40-year-olds who own or are considering investments found 65% spotted ‘this is your only chance’ as a classic horror warning sign. But when faced with a ‘last chance to buy’ investment opportunity, only 36% said it would make them more cautious, while 37% said they would feel pressure to buy quickly or risk missing out. The pattern also holds for other pressure tactics. While 59% recognised countdowns like the ticking clock in 'Saw' as a tactic designed to make characters act rashly, just 5% said they would be suspicious of the pressure created by a rising investment price graph.Blind spots show up with novelty, too. publications.title: ESMA publishes latest edition of its newsletter
publications.summary: ESMA publishes latest edition of its newsletter 29 October 2026 ESMA newsletter The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, has published today the latest edition of its Spotlight on Markets newsletter , covering key activities and publications from September and October 2026. This edition opens with the appointment of Carlo Comporti as ESMA’s next Chair . His appointment was confirmed by the Council of the European Union, and he will take up his position on 1 November 2026. Top news highlights include ESMA’s 2027 Annual Work Programme , setting out priorities for stronger, simpler and more integrated EU capital markets; the new Union Strategic Supervisory Priority on digital innovation; and the European Supervisory Authorities’ priorities for 2027 . publications.title: ESMA proposes simpler EU Taxonomy reporting
publications.summary: ESMA proposes simpler EU Taxonomy reporting 29 October 2026 Issuer disclosure Sustainable finance The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, has published its Final Report providing technical advice to the European Commission on simplifying key performance indicators under the Taxonomy Disclosures Delegated Act. ESMA recommends narrowing the mandatory operating expenditure (OpEx) KPI to non-capitalised research and development expenditure. It also proposes simpler group Taxonomy reporting, including removing the weighted-average KPI, and targeted measures to make disclosures more proportionate, clearer and easier to use. The Technical Advice was coordinated with the other European Supervisory Authorities, in particular on the voluntary use of counterparties’ OpEx information and group-level Taxonomy reporting.
